digest.component_or_area: Jira reconciler — three-way-merge baseline and field arbitration
propositions: The reconciler baseline is advanced from the last-FETCHED snapshot rather than the last-SYNCED value, causing it to lag rebar's own outbound push by exactly one pass

Local status changes (reopens, unclaims) that revert to a pre-push value are silently clobbered when inbound reads Jira's pushed value in the next pass, because the stale baseline makes the guard falsely believe local is unchanged
The _suppressed_by_inbound guard's premise 'local == baseline implies local did not change' is false for fields pushed outbound in the current pass, until baseline advances in the next pass
Per-mutation success must gate the baseline advance to avoid recording a sync that never happened when a push soft-fails (illegal transition, 400 comment-fallback), which would mask divergence

All five inbound-mirrored fields (summary, description, priority, status, assignee) share the same guard and ABA exposure, and the fix must apply to all five or document the restriction with justification

The direction-preservation regression test for status driven off adapters/jira/outbound_fields._diff_fields has no production caller, leaving the live path uncovered; cells must drive the actual outbound_field_diff.diff_canonical_fields path with explicit reachability assertions
